clue.text: Nosy creature joins Lancs community in street with personal club

parts.note: the shrew has a long pointed snout, so it is literally nosy

indicators.note: the town sits in the middle of the street abbreviation, between its two letters

parts.note: Bury is a town in Lancashire (Lancs)
something personal is your own

explanation.surface: A prying animal joins a Lancashire town's street that has its own private club.
explanation.walkthrough: BURY is a Lancashire town; it sits between S and T. Shrewsbury Town is the football club of Shrewsbury, a Shropshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: A football club, the professional side that plays in Shropshire's county town.

clue.text: Discover Paris, say, avoiding Louvre at first

indicators.note: avoiding means a letter is dropped from the surname

parts.note: Paris Hilton is the hotel heiress and celebrity, so Paris is an example of a Hilton

indicators.note: at first takes just the opening letter of the word Louvre

explanation.surface: A tourist finds their way round Paris while skipping the Louvre to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris, say' looks like the French capital, but it stands for the celebrity Paris Hilton; 'avoiding' drops L, the first letter of Louvre, from HILTON.
explanation.definitionFit: To stumble upon an idea is to discover it; the phrasal verb means find by chance.

clue.text: Oxygen needed for rearmost European in football team on plane, one flapping

indicators.note: needed for rearmost means oxygen takes the place of the hindmost of the two E letters in the team word

parts.note: a football side has eleven players, so it is an eleven
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A footballer on a flight needs oxygen while one player flaps about.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap acts on the last E of ELEVEN, the one at the rear of the team word, giving ELEVON.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevon is a hinged control surface on an aircraft wing, combining elevator and aileron, that moves up and down.

clue.text: Son on enclosed land pushes part of engine

definitions.note: singular, as each of these plugs is one part of an engine

parts.note: a park is an area of enclosed land
to plug a product is to push or promote it

explanation.surface: A boy on a fenced field shoves a piece of machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: Spark plugs ignite the fuel mixture in a petrol motor's cylinders, so they are components of it.

clue.text: Beneath Yorkshire river lies a waste product

indicators.note: in a down entry the letter written below comes after the river name

parts.note: the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire
the letter a is taken as written

explanation.surface: Below a Yorkshire river lies some refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is the nitrogen compound the body excretes in urine, a metabolic waste.

clue.text: Language homework written up before meal

indicators.note: in a down entry, written up means the letters run upwards, so backwards

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work done on one's home
a dish is a meal or course

explanation.surface: A language exercise is set before dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'homework' means DIY here, not school homework; 'written up' turns it to YID in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Yiddish is the Germanic tongue of Ashkenazi Jews, written in Hebrew script.

clue.text: Reportedly fulfil promise to nobleman, as an interim payment

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are said aloud and sound like the entry

parts.note: to fulfil a promise is to honour it, and a count is a nobleman, giving honour count

explanation.surface: Someone says they kept their word to an aristocrat by paying part of the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: With the H dropped, as usual in speech, 'honour count' sounds like the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid on account is a part payment made before the full sum is settled.

clue.text: Awful panto material beginning to nark film actress

indicators.note: awful means the letters of panto material are in a terrible mess, ready to be rearranged
beginning to takes the first letter of the word nark

explanation.surface: Dreadful pantomime script starts to irritate a movie star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges PANTO MATERIAL into NATALIEPORTMA, and the N that starts 'nark' finishes the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Natalie Portman is the Oscar-winning star of Black Swan and the Star Wars prequels.

clue.text: Bogus reptile's followed by press wanting juicy fodder

indicators.note: followed by puts the publisher's abbreviation after the earlier pieces

parts.note: mock means imitation or bogus
a turtle is a reptile
the apostrophe s supplies a letter S
OUP is Oxford University Press

explanation.surface: A fake reptile's story is chased by newspapers hungry for scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like the newspapers but is OUP, Oxford University Press.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock turtle soup is a broth made with calf's head in imitation of real turtle soup, so it is food you drink.

clue.text: Mercenary's tone changed around border with Alaska

indicators.note: around means the reshuffled letters surround the other pieces
changed means the letters of tone are rearranged

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment
AK is the postal abbreviation for Alaska

explanation.surface: A soldier of fortune's manner shifts near the Alaskan frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges the letters of 'tone' to ONTE, and 'around' wraps them round the other two pieces; AK is the US postal code for Alaska.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the make is out for profit or personal gain, as a hired soldier is.

clue.text: Did traffic here in Kent head for tunnel?

parts.note: Deal is a coastal town in Kent

indicators.note: head for takes the first letter of the word tunnel

explanation.surface: Did vehicles in a Kent town make for the Channel Tunnel?
explanation.walkthrough: DEAL is a seaside town in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To traffic is to trade, often illegally, so having trafficked is having dealt.

clue.text: Details left when splitting two grand for family members

indicators.note: when splitting means the details and left go between the two thousands, parting them

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, a grand, so two grand is two K's
info means details or information

explanation.surface: The particulars left once two thousand pounds is divided among relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinfolk are a person's relatives, the people of their own kin.

clue.text: Banker hedging is central part of process of the Treasury

indicators.note: hedging means surrounding, like a hedge round a field

parts.note: a river has banks, so in crosswords a banker is a river, here the Fal in Cornwall

indicators.note: central part of takes the middle letter of the word process

explanation.surface: A financier is cautious about a key stage in government spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' suggests money, but it is a river: the Fal in Cornwall, which goes around IS and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal describes government revenue and spending, the business of a treasury.

clue.text: Ice cream company with large plant having time and place for financiers

parts.note: Wall's is a British ice cream brand
a tree is a large plant

explanation.surface: An ice cream firm with a big factory makes room for bankers.
explanation.walkthrough: WALL'S is a well-known British ice cream brand; 'plant' is a tree, not a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall Street is the Manhattan street that stands for the American financial markets.

clue.text: Speed merchant possibly back playing rivals in rugby

indicators.note: back means the combined letters are read backwards
in places the bridge rivals inside the rugby abbreviation

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union
at bridge East and South sit as opponents, so E and S are rivals at play

explanation.surface: A fast winger perhaps returns to play against opponents in a rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed merchant' looks like a fast runner, but means someone who takes the drug speed; E and S as bridge players go into RU, and 'back' reverses RESU.
explanation.definitionFit: A taker of the amphetamine speed is a drug consumer, a merchant of it only in the loose sense of a habitual dealer in it.

clue.text: Copper, maybe covering operation, going off to unify

indicators.note: covering means the element wraps round the operation

parts.note: copper is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A policeman, perhaps shielding a covert raid, leaves to bring people together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer, but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An elopement is a couple running away in secret to marry, uniting them in wedlock.

clue.text: Open bare pad perhaps, creating novel

parts.note: bleak describes open, bare, exposed country
pad is slang for one's home, for example a house

explanation.surface: An exposed, empty flat gives rise to something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like 'new' but is the noun; Bleak House is Dickens's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak House is a Charles Dickens novel about the Jarndyce lawsuit, so it is an example of a novel.

clue.text: Very tense thug occupying sacred environment

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: occupying means the hooligan settles inside the sacred word

parts.note: holy means sacred
a rough is a violent hooligan

explanation.surface: A nervous hooligan takes over a holy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective about the thug but is T.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoroughly and very both mean completely or extremely, as in thoroughly tired.

clue.text: Kit and American inside look here for Oriental art

indicators.note: inside places the kit and American between the letters of the call

parts.note: oi is the British call of look here!
rig means kit or gear

explanation.surface: Equipment and an American inside: look at this Eastern art form.
explanation.walkthrough: OI is a British exclamation to get someone's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese craft of folding paper into figures, an art from the Far East.

clue.text: German maybe over the limit taking the wheel?

indicators.note: taking means the excess word is followed by the round letter

parts.note: OTT stands for over the top, excessive or beyond the limit
a wheel is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Is a German drunk behind the wheel?
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the limit' suggests drink-driving, but it is OTT, over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German man's name, so a German might be named it.

clue.text: Keep limited fence perhaps in sheep's boundary

indicators.note: in puts the criminal between those outer letters
the boundary of the word sheep is its first and last letters

parts.note: a fence, a dealer in stolen goods, is a criminal, a crim

explanation.surface: Keep a fence within the edge of a sheep field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fence' sounds agricultural but is a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to be sparing, keeping spending low.

clue.text: Going over line in Decline and Fall that affects pupil

indicators.note: going over means the whole is turned over and read backwards
in puts the line inside the decline word

parts.note: to die is to decline and fall away
a ley is a line, as in ley line

explanation.surface: A teacher goes through a passage of Waugh's Decline and Fall that moves a schoolboy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline and Fall' looks like Evelyn Waugh's novel but is one definition of a verb; 'Going over' reverses DILEYE. A ley line is a supposed straight alignment of ancient sites.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin over the eye closes and opens over the pupil.

clue.text: Large meal male rabbit doesn't start, with hawk hanging round?

indicators.note: hanging round means the hawk word surrounds the shortened rabbit

parts.note: to hawk goods is to tout them

indicators.note: doesn't start means the opening letter is dropped from the rabbit word

parts.note: a buck is a male rabbit

explanation.surface: A buck rabbit lingers over a feast while a hawk circles overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hawk' looks like a bird but means sell; 'doesn't start' leaves UCK. Tuck is British schoolboy slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuck-out is British slang for a big blowout meal, a hearty feed.

clue.text: Postman regularly avoided travel in Antipodean region

indicators.note: regularly avoided means every other letter of Postman is skipped, from the first

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: The mailman steadily stayed away from travelling to a far-flung region.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is a region of New Zealand's South Island, down under.

clue.text: Food course

definitions.meaning: a course or line of action, also a sailing course

explanation.definitionFit: Tack means grub, as in sailors' hardtack, and also a direction taken, as when a yacht sails close-hauled.

clue.text: Ancient character, many years doctor, retired

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: an age is a long period of years
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: An old figure, a doctor for many years, has stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, a letter from antiquity.

clue.text: Musical style from player covering Clapton that's embraced by drivers

indicators.note: embraced by means the result goes inside the motoring letters

parts.note: the AA is the British Automobile Association, an organisation of drivers

indicators.note: covering means the player wraps round the guitarist's first name

parts.note: a man is a player in a team or a game piece
Eric Clapton is the blues-rock guitarist

explanation.surface: A style from a musician doing a cover of Eric Clapton that motorists love.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the UK's Automobile Association, a motoring organisation; 'covering' is not a cover version.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana is a roots genre mixing country, folk and blues traditions.

clue.text: Medical specialist perfectly wrenches neck, turning digit

parts.note: to know something off pat is to know it perfectly
to rick is to sprain or wrench

indicators.note: turning means the cuddle word is read backwards

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle, to pet
a toe is a digit

explanation.surface: A doctor neatly twists someone's neck and then their toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neck' is the verb, to pet; 'turning' reverses it to TEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrick Steptoe was the British gynaecologist who pioneered IVF, achieving the first test-tube baby in 1978.
